successCriteria.description: A repository test asserts that when `findByQuery` receives a non-empty `employeeIds` array, the generated SQL contains an `employee_id = ANY($n)` condition and the array is passed as a single parameter value (not spread into individual placeholders), with the placeholder index consistent with the other conditions.
A repository test asserts that when `employeeIds` is absent or an empty array, `findByQuery` emits no `employee_id` condition (no `ANY` clause) and returns rows unfiltered by employee.

Service tests assert `list` role scoping: EMPLOYEE delegates to `repository.findByQuery` with `employeeIds = [actor.id]`; MANAGER with `[actor.id, ...directReportIds]` where direct reports come from `employeeService.getEmployeesByManagerId(actor.id)` (one level, not transitive); ADMIN with no `employeeIds` filter.

Service tests assert `list` merges the scoped `employeeIds` into the query (overriding any client-supplied value for EMPLOYEE/MANAGER) and delegates to `repository.findByQuery` exactly once, returning its result unchanged.

Service tests assert `getById` returns the request when visible and throws `NotFoundError('Leave request not found')` with the identical message for a null request AND for a request whose `employeeId` is outside the actor's visibility scope, with visibility status-independent (a manager sees a direct report's request in every status).

Route tests assert `GET /leaves` parses/validates query params (status/leaveTypeCode enum membership, the four date bounds via the existing `toDate` helper, limit/offset as integers) and returns 200 with the array; invalid params yield a 400 `ValidationError` mapped through `sendError`.

Route tests assert `GET /leaves/:id` returns 200 with the single request, and that a `NotFoundError` from the service is mapped via `sendError` to a 404 `{ error, code }` body (the same 404 for invisible and nonexistent ids).
The new tests pass under the project's Jest runner (`npx jest`) and do not modify any production source file under `src/` — the 6.1/6.2 deliverables are treated as fixed contracts.

constraints: This sub-phase is test-only: no production source under `src/` may be modified. The repository/service/routes delivered in 6.1 and 6.2 are fixed contracts to be asserted against, not changed.

Repository `findByQuery` tests must exercise the real `PgLeaveRequestRepository` (or a subclass) against a fake `dbPool`/`PoolClient` that captures the SQL text and parameter array — they must not re-implement the query logic in a fake repository, or the `employee_id = ANY($n)` single-parameter invariant is untested.

Service tests must use in-memory fakes for the injected collaborators (matching the existing `leave.service.test.ts` pattern) and must not open a transaction or forward a `PoolClient` — `list`/`getById` are read-only.

Route tests must follow the existing `leave.routes.test.ts` seam: register `leaveRoutes` on a Fastify instance decorated with a fake `leaveService` and a `preHandler` that sets `request.user`, and inject requests — no real DB, no real auth token.

Tests must not assert implementation shape (no assertions on private helper names, SQL string literals beyond the `ANY`/single-parameter invariant, or route internals) — only the observable contracts.
outOfScope: Implementing or modifying `findByQuery`, `list`, `getById`, or the GET routes — those are owned by sibling sub-phases 6.1/6.2 and are already delivered; this sub-phase only tests them.
The `POST /leaves`, submit/approve/reject/cancel endpoints and their existing tests — already covered; this sub-phase adds only the read-surface tests.
The `GET /employees/me`, `GET /balances/me`, and `POST /auth/login` surfaces and their tests (Phase 7 / other phases) — not part of the leave read surface.
End-to-end smoke-check assertions over real HTTP (scripts/smoke.js) — that belongs to Phase 7, not this unit/integration test sub-phase.

ambiguities.description: How to exercise the real `PgLeaveRequestRepository.findByQuery` without a live PostgreSQL database.
options: Inject a fake `dbPool`/`PoolClient` whose `query(sql, values)` records the SQL text and parameter array, then assert on the captured values
Subclass `PgLeaveRequestRepository` and override `db()` to return a recording client
Use an in-memory fake repository that re-implements the ANY logic (NOT recommended — would not test the real code)

ambiguities.description: Where the new tests should live given the existing files already cover the leave module.
options: Extend the existing `tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.service.test.ts` and `leave.routes.test.ts` with new describe blocks
Add a new `tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.repository.test.ts` for the repository and extend the two existing files for service/routes

entityInvariants.invariant: Visibility is status-independent: a MANAGER may read a direct report's request in every status (DRAFT/SUBMITTED/APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED); visibility is governed solely by the employee-id scope (EMPLOYEE self, MANAGER self + one-level direct reports, ADMIN all), never by status.

A request the caller may not see is indistinguishable from one that does not exist: `getById` returns the same `NotFoundError('Leave request not found')` for both a null lookup and an out-of-scope `employeeId`.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Read-only; returns an array (possibly empty); never throws on empty results. When `params.employeeIds` is a non-empty array it is pushed as a single parameter for an `employee_id = ANY($n)` condition; when absent/empty no employee filter is applied.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Requires an authenticated actor (missing/invalid actor → UnauthorizedError/ForbiddenError); scopes results by role (EMPLOYEE self, MANAGER self + one-level direct reports, ADMIN all) and delegates to repository.findByQuery.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Read-only; never opens a transaction or forwards a PoolClient; returns the repository result unchanged.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Requires an authenticated actor; visibility scoped by role (same rule as list).
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Throws NotFoundError('Leave request not found') for a null request AND for an out-of-scope request (identical response); read-only, no transaction.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The `NotFoundError('Leave request not found')` message asserted in `getById` tests must match the exact string thrown by `LeaveService.getById` (and the repository's `update`/`findById` conventions) in `src/modules/leave/leave.service.ts`.

The `employee_id = ANY($n)` single-parameter behaviour asserted in repository tests must match the implementation in `PgLeaveRequestRepository.findByQuery` (array pushed as one value, condition appended before LIMIT/OFFSET).

Route tests must reuse the existing `resolveActor`/`sendError`/`toDate`/`parseListQuery` behaviour and the `fastify.leaveService` decoration seam exactly as in the existing route test file, asserting the same error/status mapping.

Service tests must reuse the existing in-memory fake pattern and fixtures (FakeLeaveRepository, FakeEmployeeService, makeActor/makeEmployee/makeRequest) from the existing leave service test, extending `FakeLeaveRepository.findByQuery` to record the received params rather than ignoring them.
The `LeaveRequestQueryParams.employeeIds` type and `LeaveStatus`/`LeaveTypeCode` enum members referenced in tests must match `src/shared/types/index.ts` (the Phase 1 extension).

integrationPoints.why: The repository test drives the real implementation through its injected `dbPool` to capture the SQL and parameter array, proving the `employee_id = ANY($n)` single-parameter invariant.
The service tests exercise the real `LeaveService` with in-memory fakes to assert role scoping, delegation, and the identical NotFoundError for invisible/missing requests.
The route tests inject requests through a Fastify instance with a fake `leaveService` to assert query parsing/validation, 200 responses, and `sendError` mapping.
